header: Date: 2027-07-15 | Time: 10:00-10:48 UTC | Duration: ~48m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CSM) — Lena Park (Harborline Head of ML), Marcus Bell (CTO), Sofia Ruiz (Product), Daniel Cho (SRE)
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on recent regression spike for the customer-support prompt set after quantization changes. Reviewed scorecard diffs, discussed failure-mode runbook (rollback triggers, alert thresholds), and agreed next steps: targeted regression runs, security docs, and a canary throughput test on Dedicated. Some verbal confusion around KV cache vs K-V cash in the transcript; also brief pricing pushback from customer on burst vs reserved capacity.
topics: Regression spike analysis for quantized model
Prompt set scoring and false-positive handling
Pricing options: Dedicated reserved vs burst
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: alright everyone, uh good morning, thanks for joining, this is our weekly POC sync with Harborline, um Ethan and I are here from Redwood and Priya will take notes. quick round robin?
00:12 Lena Park: hi, lena here, will kick us off with the recent failures, we've seen a bump in hallucinations after the last 4-bit quant-change.
00:22 Marcus Bell: yeah i can share a short summary from infra — p95 latency is okay but quality score dropped 8 points on the customer-support set.
00:30 Ethan Ruiz: okay thanks, uh are we confident the test harness is reusing the same tokenization? sometimes tokenizers shift with quantization experiments, i know it's dumb but we've seen that before.
00:44 Lena Park: good call — tokenizer was consistent, we double-checked. We ran v1.2-fp16 vs v1.3-quant4 and the delta is in the exactness of entity linking.
00:58 Sofia Ruiz: and for PM context, those failing examples are mostly multi-turn agent handoffs where the model invents account numbers. That's our main safety concern.
01:12 Ethan Ruiz: right, that explains the false positive spike in the scorecard. just to be explicit: are these outputs triggering the \"sensitive-data\" guardrail or the model is just hallucinating but not flagged?
01:25 Lena Park: most are not flagged because the guardrail is an NER-based heuristic, it misses inferred numbers.
01:35 Maya Chen: okay so we need to consider two levers: expand guardrail signals (NER + pattern match + checksum heuristics) and adjust scoring thresholds temporarily while we triage.
01:47 Marcus Bell: and we want a concrete runbook — when do we rollback to fp16? what's the trigger?
01:55 Ethan Ruiz: proposal — if top-line false-positive rate for critical intents increases by >5% and customer-visible incidents exceed 3/day, trigger automatic rollback to last stable variant. we can automate that in the console as a rule.
02:12 Daniel Cho: would rollback mean shifting traffic to Redwood Hosted or Dedicated fp16 pool? our preference is to stay in the Dedicated reserved pool if possible, but need to understand cost delta.
02:25 Maya Chen: good point. Dedicated supports immediate variant fallback, but there's a small warm-up cost if we move between variants — KV cache will be cold initially, so short-term latency may spike.
02:40 Daniel Cho: K-V cash? (laughs) i heard 'K-V cash' in the notes earlier — yeah cold cache is a concern.
02:50 Ethan Ruiz: ha yeah, we sometimes see transcribe write K-V cash. but yes KV cache cold starts can add 50-150ms p95 for the first few minutes depending on sequence length.
03:05 Lena Park: can we quantify impact? we need numbers for our SREs.
03:10 Ethan Ruiz: absolutely — we'll run a 2-hour canary throughput run on Dedicated and capture p50/p95/p99 and token cost delta with and without warm cache. that'll be part of the next steps.
03:22 Sofia Ruiz: on scoring: can you walk through how Redwood's scorecard flags these? Are we using BLEU-like heuristics or more semantic similarity?
03:33 Ethan Ruiz: scorecard uses a mix: token-overlap metrics for strict intents, semantic embeddings distance for paraphrase tolerance, and custom tests for blacklisted patterns. for the failed cases we saw the embedding-distance still within threshold which is why they slipped through.
03:48 Marcus Bell: so we should update the scoring to weight the checksum heuristics higher for account-number-like slots.
03:55 Maya Chen: agreed. Lena, can you share a sample of 1,500 failing queries with annotations? that will let us craft a targeted test and tune the weights.
04:05 Lena Park: yes, i'll drop that in the shared folder after the call.
04:10 Priya Nair: note — link to shared assets will be recorded in the deck; Maya will follow up.
04:20 Marcus Bell: on the commercial side, we're still trying to decide between reserved capacity vs burst. our cost model is tight — burst seems cheaper short-term but less predictable.
04:32 Maya Chen: understood. we can provide a two-tier commit proposal: a small reserved baseline for predictable throughput + burst credits for spikes. i'll send numbers for both.
04:42 Sofia Ruiz: any security ask? we need to confirm KMS and audit logs for Private.
04:48 Maya Chen: yes, we support KMS integrations and full audit logs in Private. i'll include SOC2 summary and KMS setup steps.
04:56 Daniel Cho: and for VPC peering, we need Redwood's egress IP ranges and a contact for net-ops.
05:03 Maya Chen: we'll include that — Daniel, can you provision a test peering window next week?
05:10 Daniel Cho: yes aiming for 2027-07-19, i'll confirm after this meeting.
05:16 Ethan Ruiz: back to regression: i recommend a narrow A/B test — run quant4 on 20% traffic against fp16 baseline for 24h with real traffic tape, then compare scorecard and user-visible incidents.
05:29 Lena Park: that would be perfect, but can we run it against sanitized logs? we have PII concerns.
05:36 Ethan Ruiz: yes, we can run the evaluation on an anonymized tape; Redwood has a sanitized-run workflow that strips PII before scoring.
05:44 Marcus Bell: what's the expected time for Ethan to run the regression on the prompt set?
05:49 Ethan Ruiz: i can start the automated regression today and will aim to share a detailed report by 2027-07-20. it'll include token counts, p95 latency, false-positive breakdown, and prompt-level diffs.
06:02 Sofia Ruiz: during the last run, some of the transcript timestamps were off and the speech-to-text mislabelled Redwood product names, just FYI when you send notes.
06:12 Maya Chen: thanks for flag — we'll be explicit in the follow-up.
06:18 Lena Park: small question — do we support incremental guardrail rules via the Console or do we need a deployment?
06:24 Ethan Ruiz: most guardrail weight changes are config-only and can be pushed via console for quick iterations; structural checks like checksum validators may require a small code push, but we have a fast path.
06:36 Marcus Bell: okay, let's recap next steps.
06:40 Maya Chen: recap: Ethan runs regression on v1.3-quant4 vs v1.2-fp16, deliver report by 7/20; Maya sends pricing and SOC2/KMS notes by 7/18; Daniel confirms VPC peering window by 7/19; Lena drops annotated failures by 7/21; schedule canary cup — aim for 7/23.
06:58 Sofia Ruiz: sounds good. thanks everyone.
07:02 Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in email, end call.
07:08 [meeting ended]
